title: Elodie and the Semester
premise: Mirabel Zhou has perfected the art of being unnoticed at Halloway Prep, letting his bread do the talking at his family's struggling bakery. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving him notes in ink that vanishes by morning, he's pulled into a decades-old mystery: the ghost is a former student, silenced after exposing a theft that founded the school's prestige. As Mirabel investigates with the help of prom committee queen Priya Anand, he uncovers that the current headmaster's family built their fortune on the cover-up. In the end, Mirabel must choose between protecting his scholarship and the bakery's lease — both controlled by the school — and telling the truth, and he chooses truth, reading the ghost's final letter aloud at prom, costing him the scholarship but earning him a community that finally sees him, and a new bakery funded by the town he dared to speak for.
about_author: Rosalind Hartwell is a former school librarian who spent ten years cataloging the secrets students left in returned books. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover that silence is a choice, not a personality.

chapters.title: The Rye That Says Sorry
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He bakes an apology loaf for a teacher he accidentally offended, establishing his habit of baking feelings. At school he's invisible by design. Emotional beat: the comfort of being overlooked — and the first hairline crack of loneliness in it.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A note appears in his locker addressed 'Mirabel' — his name, spelled right, in ink that fades by third period. He assumes a prank. Emotional beat: unease curdling into a thrill he doesn't want to admit to.

chapters.title: The Legend of Halloway's Ghost
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He researches the school ghost, a 1970s student who vanished before graduation. His best friend Dev warns him to drop it. Emotional beat: curiosity versus the survival instinct of the invisible kid.

chapters.title: Priya Anand Has a List
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The prom committee president notices Mirabel's bakery invoice discrepancy and confronts him — and catches him pocketing a second ghost note. Emotional beat: two careful people recognizing each other's carefulness.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Second Period
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An uneasy alliance forms over sourdough in the bakery's back room; Priya reveals the ghost's notes have appeared before, always to students about to leave. Emotional beat: the first real conversation Mirabel has had in years.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Print
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the archives, they find the ghost's name scratched out of the 1974 yearbook. The headmaster catches them and offers Mirabel a 'library internship' — a bribe dressed as a gift. Emotional beat: the chill of being seen by the wrong person.

chapters.title: The Lease on Linden Street
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He discovers the bakery's lease renewal depends on the school's goodwill — his father's livelihood is collateral. Emotional beat: the weight of duty pressing down on a boy who wanted to stay light.

chapters.title: Notes in Vanishing Ink
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The notes escalate, naming names: teachers who looked away, a donation that bought the science wing. Priya, whose mother is on the school board, feels the ground tilt. Emotional beat: loyalty to family versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Dev, Who Knew First
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dev admits he received a note last year and burned it out of fear. His guilt and anger fracture their friendship. Emotional beat: the cost of silence, paid in friendship.

chapters.title: The Ghost Has a Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They identify the ghost: Elias Wren, expelled in 1974 after accusing the school's benefactor — the current headmaster's grandfather — of embezzling the endowment. Emotional beat: the ghost becomes a boy, not a story.

chapters.title: Bread for the Dead
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He bakes a memorial loaf using a recipe from Elias's mother, found in an old community cookbook, and leaves it at the sealed music room. A new note appears: 'Thank you.' Emotional beat: grief offered as flour and salt.

chapters.title: Prom Court Politics
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The headmaster pressures Priya to keep Mirabel away from prom planning, dangling her college recommendation. She agrees — and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: complicity, and the moment she decides to stop.

chapters.title: The Science Wing's Foundation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the money, they find the 1974 endowment ledger hidden in plain sight, digitized into the library's founding exhibit. The theft is documented. Emotional beat: triumph that arrives with dread, because proof is dangerous.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Mirabel Home
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A car idles outside the bakery; his father's lease paperwork arrives early, with new clauses. The headmaster's message is clear. Emotional beat: fear for family, the one lever that always works.

chapters.title: The Fight in the Flour Aisle
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Dev, scared for Mirabel, tells the headmaster about the ledger to protect him. Mirabel explodes — the invisible kid finally shouting. Emotional beat: betrayal that is also love, which is the worst kind.

chapters.title: What Priya Burned
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confesses she once found a note two years ago and reported it to the headmaster, who made it disappear. Her guilt mirrors Dev's. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit — everyone has chosen loyalty over truth at least once.

chapters.title: Elias Wren, Alive Enough
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They track down Elias Wren living quietly two towns over, an old man who says he stopped fighting because no one would listen to a baker's son. He gives them his original letter. Emotional beat: the ghost handing his unfinished sentence to the living.

chapters.title: The Week Before Prom
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Reconciliation with Dev; the plan forms — read Elias's letter at prom, when every family in town will be in the gym. Mirabel's father, told everything, chooses to stand with his son. Emotional beat: the labels coming off, one by one.

chapters.title: The Gymnasium, Lit Gold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Prom begins. Priya, as committee head, controls the microphone. The headmaster watches Mirabel like a hawk. Emotional beat: held breath, chaperoned joy, the storm before the sentence.

chapters.title: The Letter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Priya cues the music down; Mirabel takes the mic and reads Elias Wren's letter — the theft, the expulsion, the erased name. The room fractures. The headmaster moves to cut the power; parents stop him. Emotional beat: the climax — truth spoken outside any courtroom, at full volume.

chapters.title: Aftermath, in Plain Ink
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board investigates; the headmaster resigns; the scholarship is 'restructured' out from under Mirabel, exactly as threatened. But the town, the teachers, and Elias himself rally. Emotional beat: justice that costs, and is worth it.

chapters.title: The Loaf That Says Stay
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Graduation week: the bakery reopens with community investment, Elias Wren's name restored to a plaque, and a final note in permanent ink: 'You were never invisible.' Mirabel bakes a loaf that says stay — and means it for himself. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and chosen.
